title: Configurable simulation campaign runner
description:
## Problem

Simulation campaigns are hardcoded in example binaries (`grand_phase1_sims.rs`, `grand_phase3_sim.rs`). Each binary runs a fixed set of curves sequentially with hardcoded parameters. There is no way to:

- Run a single curve without running all others
- Change parameters (SNR range, min_errors, decoder config) without editing source
- Define new simulation campaigns without writing new Rust code
- Compose campaigns from reusable curve definitions

The resume feature helps avoid redundant work, but the fundamental problem is that simulation campaigns are not configurable.

## Proposed Solution

A TOML-based simulation campaign configuration that a generic runner binary reads and executes.

### Campaign config format

```toml
[campaign]
name = "phase1_fig3"
output_dir = "dev/simulation_results"

[[curve]]
name = "fig3_ebch_product"
code_type = "product"
component = "ebch_16_11"
decoder = "turbo_sogrand"
decoder_params = { max_iterations = 20, alpha = 0.5, list_size = 4 }
snr_range = { start = 0.0, stop = 4.0, step = 0.5 }
min_errors = 100
max_frames = 500_000

[[curve]]
name = "fig3_ldpc_nms"
code_type = "nr5g_ldpc"
code_params = { base_graph = 2, n = 256, k = 121 }
decoder = "nms"
decoder_params = { scale = 0.75 }
snr_range = { start = 0.0, stop = 4.0, step = 0.5 }
min_errors = 100
max_frames = 500_000
```

### Runner binary

```bash
# Run all curves in a campaign
cargo run -p gf2-coding --release --all-features --bin sim_runner -- campaign.toml

# Run a single curve by name
cargo run -p gf2-coding --release --all-features --bin sim_runner -- campaign.toml --curve fig3_ldpc_sp

# Run with parallel SNR sweep
cargo run -p gf2-coding --release --all-features --bin sim_runner -- campaign.toml --parallel
```

### Features

- Each curve is independently runnable via `--curve` filter
- Resume from existing CSV (already implemented in SimulationRunner)
- Parallel SNR sweep via `--parallel` flag
- Campaign configs checked into `dev/campaigns/` for reproducibility
- The existing hardcoded examples become thin wrappers or are replaced entirely

## Success Criteria

- [ ] TOML campaign config format defined and parsed
- [ ] Generic `sim_runner` binary reads config and executes curves
- [ ] `--curve` flag to select individual curves
- [ ] `--parallel` flag for parallel SNR sweep
- [ ] Phase 1 and Phase 3 campaigns expressed as TOML configs
- [ ] Existing hardcoded examples either removed or converted to use the config
- [ ] All existing tests pass
